Development

All repository documentation, code comments, diagnostics, commit messages, and website content are maintained in English.

Run checks

The native workspace uses Rust with wgpu. CI checks both Windows and Linux with the stable Rust toolchain. Native fixtures require no game content:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo build --workspace --locked
python tools/check_native_parity.py --native target/debug/openasc

Use target/debug/openasc.exe on Windows. Native/Python contract checks compare original KN5 fixtures, selection, transforms/bounds, full material properties/sampler mappings, INI values/order/source lines, LUT samples, static model declarations, packed/unpacked vehicle configurations and rejection codes. Optional repeated --model PATH arguments compare locally installed models without copying them. --car PATH/TO/content/cars/CAR additionally compares complete local vehicle configuration values and field sources. Warning wording/order is not compared; Rust fixtures separately check warning codes. Agreement between two openASC implementations does not establish original-simulator parity.

Unpacked-directory fixtures also compare car_data_name_ignored counts when unrelated conflict-copy/nonportable files accompany valid resources. Preserve strict validation of requested names and whole-source selection when changing this behavior. The directory-entry budget includes ignored files and subdirectories; enumeration must remain bounded before sorting. See index validation.

The separate GPU test is explicitly opt-in on a machine with a native adapter:

cargo test -p asc-render --locked --test gpu --test track_textures -- --ignored --nocapture

Five single-model GPU tests check non-background geometry, occlusion independent of triangle order, non-aligned row readback, PNG pixels/overwrite refusal, UV orientation, opaque versus cutout alpha, opacity and linear-light blending, read-only/disabled depth and back-to-front transparency ordering. Another GPU test checks BC1/2/3 direct upload against a device created without BC support, including alpha and authored non-power-of-two/sub-block mip tails. Two multilayer GPU tests check linear unnormalised RGBA weights, magic gain, alpha-as-a-fourth-weight and world-XZ versus source-UV coordinates. A separate composition GPU test proves that two composed models with identical texture names retain distinct red/green pixels. CPU fixtures cover native config parsing, translation and rebasing, resource confinement, model/texture budgets and per-model resource isolation. Set OPENASC_TEST_FALLBACK=1 to request a software adapter; Linux CI installs Mesa Vulkan and runs these tests explicitly. GPU adapter absence fails the explicit tests. Structural, DDS and resource-resolution tests remain GPU-independent. Cargo build outputs under target/ are ignored; commit Cargo.lock with dependency changes.

Six explicit desktop tests require a display: four scene/material inspection fixtures, a car/track composition fixture and a coupled native-drive fixture:

cargo test -p asc-app --locked --test window -- --ignored --nocapture

Linux CI installs mesa-vulkan-drivers, xvfb and libxkbcommon-x11-0, then runs it under Xvfb with software Vulkan. The X11 window backend requires the xkbcommon X11 runtime library. It verifies one uncaptured presentation and four presented/read-back frames, real window resize to 640 by 480, changed camera matrices, BGRA-to-RGBA PNG output and changed pixels from a diffuse toggle at a fixed camera. Camera math and camera-dependent transparency order also have GPU-independent tests. This diagnostic automation does not establish real mouse/keyboard, DPI, monitor migration or device-loss recovery behavior.

Source is organised as a subsystem workspace under crates/, following the openOMSI project layout. Build the executable with cargo build -p asc-app; it is named openasc (openasc.exe on Windows). The former native/openasc-native package has been replaced by the subsystem crates. Python/WebGL research source is under tools/prototype/; the root Python package is only a compatibility entry point. See the architecture for dependency boundaries.

Python 3.10+ is enough for the tools, tests, and documentation builder. No game installation is needed for tests.

python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python tools/build_site.py --check
node --check site/app.js
node --check tools/prototype/viewer/viewer.js
node --check tools/prototype/viewer/dds.js
node --check tools/prototype/viewer/drive.js
node --test tests/test_dds.cjs

Node.js 18+ is used for JavaScript syntax checks and original DDS pixel tests. The website itself has no npm dependencies or build-time JavaScript framework.

The local geometry viewer also has no npm dependencies. Its JavaScript is in tools/prototype/viewer/, served only by python -m openasc view. Tests construct original complete KN5 fixtures and exercise the loopback server, including foreign-host/origin rejection. Binary fixtures are not copied from the game.

Update the website

python tools/build_site.py
python -m http.server 4173 --directory site --bind 127.0.0.1

Open localhost. The document builder supports the Markdown subset used here: headings, paragraphs, links, inline code, bold text, lists, fenced code, and tables. Raw HTML in documentation is escaped.

Edit docs/ for documentation, web/overview.html for the overview body, and web/layout.html for the shared shell. Edit site/style.css and site/app.js for styling and browser behavior. Generated HTML files contain a notice identifying their source.

Contribute

The independent Rust telemetry research tool is documented in TELEMETRY.md. Run cargo test --locked -p asc-telemetry for original protocol/journal fixtures and Windows named-mapping tests. Tests never create or write the game's mapping names. Keep local capture logs in ignored reports/; a complete acquisition log does not establish original physics parity.

The independent driving model is in tools/prototype/openasc/dynamics.py; its tests use original flat/sloped geometry and original car configurations. Keep rendering and HTTP telemetry reads out of the fixed-step solver. Controller tests can advance exact steps with an injected clock instead of sleeping. Real-content/browser validation remains local; record the scope and limitations before changing compatibility claims.

Website progress screenshots are selected flattened captures under site/images/, with captions in web/overview.html. Update them after meaningful visual milestones. Do not add raw game assets or temporary browser reports. The project's MIT license does not relicense the underlying game content depicted in screenshots.

Start with an issue describing a reproducible problem or bounded feature. Keep parser fixtures original and small. A green test suite does not establish compatibility with all Assetto Corsa content.

Before committing, check that neither assettocorsa/ nor reports/ is tracked. These directories are ignored intentionally. Do not include original executable files, copyrighted game content, or third-party mods.

New source code and website files use the MIT license. Dependencies and any future third-party additions must retain their own license notices.

Validate native ground preparation

The workspace tests include original analytic geometry and surface fixtures. The existing native parity script also checks static ground preparation in CI without an installed game. For optional local validation, supply track directories:

python tools/check_native_parity.py --native target/debug/openasc.exe --ground ./assettocorsa/content/tracks/drift --ground ./assettocorsa/content/tracks/magione

The command compares complete mesh/surface metadata and 1000 deterministic centroid support queries plus two misses on each track, in bounded batches. No source content is extracted or modified. This checks agreement with the research implementation; it does not validate the original game's contact or tyre model.

Validate native geometric placement

python tools/check_native_parity.py --native target/debug/openasc.exe --placement ./assettocorsa/content/cars/bmw_m3_e30 ./assettocorsa/content/tracks/drift

The ordinary CI invocation also compares original spawn/placement fixtures, packed/unpacked car loading, complete contacts, report error flags and CLI exit statuses. The optional local comparison checks every retained marker and four wheel contacts without extracting or changing content. Drift's unrelated duplicate start marker remains an error even when AC_PIT_0 has four hits. This preparation does not validate a native driving solver.

Validate the native physics kernel

cargo test --locked -p asc-physics
cargo run --locked -p asc-physics --example free_body

Both are covered by CI: the ordinary workspace tests include analytic motion/conservation/clock fixtures, and a separate step executes the original free-body example on Windows and Linux. It needs no game assets, Python or GPU. The native session bridge additionally checks explicit centre-of-mass and spawn-basis initialization. Preserve error/convergence bounds and reject partial state mutation; no original vehicle-force compatibility is implied by these kernel checks.

Validate suspension records and independent force links

cargo test --locked -p asc-physics --test spring
cargo run --locked -p asc-physics --example spring_pair
cargo test --locked -p asc-vehicle --test suspension
python tools/check_native_parity.py --native target/debug/openasc.exe --suspension ./assettocorsa/content/cars/bmw_m3_e30

CI runs the original coupled example on Windows/Linux and compares packed/unpacked suspension source records without game files. The optional local comparison checks all consumed fields and their provenance; it does not compare the original suspension solver. For multiple links sharing a body, aggregate through step_springs rather than repeatedly advancing isolated pairs. Keep automatic source-to-force mapping disabled until source frames, units and original laws have been validated.

Validate native car/track roots

The normal workspace suite includes rigid-pose and application-assembly fixtures. Explicit GPU/window checks include root-transformed normals, persistent pose updates with world transparency sorting, and a two-root native presentation fixture. They run in the existing Linux software Vulkan/Xvfb jobs.

cargo run --locked -p asc-app -- preview ./assettocorsa/content/cars/bmw_m3_e30 ./assettocorsa/content/tracks/drift/models.ini --smoke

The optional real-content smoke verifies native presentation/camera/resize/readback, not actual keyboard driving or independent physical mouse gestures. New source/capture names must remain outside tracked game content; publish only selected flattened frames with accurate scope captions.

The native-drive window fixture creates its own car/track/configuration, injects throttle/steer/brake through the shared key handler, and checks chassis motion/yaw, braking and changed surface pixels at a fixed camera. It now compares enabled/disabled articulation on eight original wheel/upright subtrees: initial pixels and chassis states agree, driven pixels differ, and wheel/upright transforms diverge. Ordinary Rust coverage is 267 tests; the explicit desktop check executes two diagnostic windows sequentially. It uses no game installation. Physical keyboard use, focus/monitor changes and real device-loss remain outside independent desktop validation. Ordinary CPU fixtures cover key release/clear/brake aliases, ignored autorepeat, smooth rack target response, forward/reverse/braking/reset behavior, invalid-input atomicity and camera-follow projection.

Source-wheel registration CPU fixtures require only original configuration literals and a synthetic KN5 header. They check nonzero linkage pose/levers and rotated chassis coordinates, selected compound radii through actual contact force, source reload behavior/provenance and malformed/ambiguous selections. The default native-drive example now uses source corner references; the ordinary explicit workbench examples remain available for independent force-law isolation.

Source reflection tests distinguish polar and axial quantities under a determinant-minus-one coordinate map. Adapter fixtures check both DWB and STRUT derivatives/reactions; the coupled application fixture tests actual reflected dynamics and contact with explicitly transformed synthetic local parameters. Keep a reflection out of quaternion/root-pose inputs. Reflecting raw hardpoints alone must never silently reflect explicit world loads, springs or inertia.

Coupled impulse fixtures cover analytic free-travel/carried-mass response, off-centre momentum and pose preservation, moving-rack work, passive normal restitution and atomic failures. CI runs cargo run --locked -p asc-physics --example coupled_impulse, an original numeric fixture needing no game files/display. It does not enable native-window collision detection or response.

Native WALL tests use only original generated mesh/collider/configuration literals. cargo test -p asc-ground --test walls, cargo test -p asc-session --test collider and cargo test -p asc-app --test wall_query need no game files or display. The CLI retains a complete result before stdout, including aggregate overflow failures. Optional real-content checks use wall-query examples/wall-query.json; source geometry/research reports stay outside tracked content. No new rendered collision behavior or screenshot is claimed by the geometry-query milestone.

The simultaneous contact core runs in cargo test -p asc-physics --test chassis; filter oblique_sliding for the independent anisotropic friction check. cargo test -p asc-app static_wall_impact exercises original geometry through the static adapter; patch_points_merge checks manifold merging and overflow. Optional local-content validation uses wall-impact examples/wall-impact.json. Treat nonconvergence as an explicit failure and inspect the reported projected residual; do not silently discard points, broaden geometry or claim penetration correction. Generated research reports and game files remain ignored.

Prescribed motion tests run with cargo test -p asc-ground --test walls and cargo test -p asc-app --test wall_query. conservative_rotation covers analytical rotation about an offset reference; swept_bounds_caps verifies unresolved paths fail. Local source inspection uses wall-sweep examples/wall-sweep.json. Keep conservative proximity events distinct from exact TOI and keep prescribed motion distinct from the force integrator's actual trajectory. No new driving screenshot is claimed by this geometry milestone.

First-event tests run in cargo test -p asc-physics --test chassis (filters selected_midpoint, fraction_selector, partial_midpoint) and cargo test -p asc-session --test wall_step. The application fixture also runs with filter static_wall_impact. Optional local content validation is wall-step examples/wall-step.json. Inspect the pre-impact integration sample separately from post-impact state when auditing impulse momentum/work. Keep callback evaluation time-based; a selected final event may precede the proposal midpoint in simulated time. An unresolved or zero-time event must never be repeatedly retried without an explicit progress/contact policy.

cargo test -p asc-physics --test chassis clustered_friction exercises distinct near-coincident contacts without changing tolerances. Filter independent_exhaustive for the independent normal complementarity reference; cargo test -p asc-app static_wall_impact now includes the strict frictional moving event. Inspect normal_projection_used rather than assuming the same iteration path succeeds for all manifolds. Preserve the original sequential trajectory, all contacts, final checks and rollback when modifying the alternate projection.

Departure coverage runs in cargo test -p asc-ground --test walls (filters full_path_axis_gap, certified_departure, departure_certificate), cargo test -p asc-session --test wall_step certified_departure, and cargo test -p asc-app --test wall_query cli_departure. Keep the opt-in behavior, strictly positive analytic bound, rotating local centre and all interior extrema. A positive initial velocity or clear endpoint is not enough to skip an obstacle. The report cap includes certificates as well as event contacts.
